person_note: The Goodreads evidence repeatedly exposes Molly as a participating “I” narrator in reflections, workplace scenes, memories, and the murder account. First-person beats embedded in dialogue-heavy quotes are consistent with that same base voice; gnomic “you” and “we” statements are not second-person or additional narrative strands. The authorized excerpt independently confirms sustained first-person narration in the prologue and opening chapter, while whole-book guides and reviews state that Molly remains the first-person narrator through the epilogue. The authorized prose is opening-only, but the numerous apparently interior quotes and explicit whole-book sources close that scope gap; no credible alternating or third-person structure was found.
